question.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x) & ⇒ & v=\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 6x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =6x\cdot \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\int \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\cdot 6\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }-2{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =2(\pi \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(3\pi )-0\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(0))+\frac{2}{3}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =2(0-0)+\frac{2}{3}(-1-1) \\  & =-\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
